I am a 55-year-old woman, and I have farmed in Quzhou County my whole life. I finished high school, which was rare for girls in my generation, so I can read the extension leaflets and understand soil-crop relationships better than many of my neighbors. My family has about 8 mu of flat, irrigable land on the North China Plain. It is early March now, and the winter wheat I sowed last October is greening up.

I will stick to the wheat–summer maize double-cropping system on all 8 mu. That is what this land and climate are built for. I considered cotton, but the labor and pesticide burden is too heavy for my family, and the price swings keep me awake at night. Wheat gives us flour for the household, and maize has a steady buyer at the local feed mill. I will not expand by renting more land; 8 mu is exactly what I can manage well with family labor and still do a careful job.

For the wheat already in the ground: I sowed an improved semi-dwarf variety last autumn with the rotary tiller. Because I understand that nitrogen alone is not enough, I will apply about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu—split as urea at green-up and again at jointing—plus 5 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potassium per mu as compound fertilizer to keep the soil from getting more depleted. Groundwater is dropping every year, so I will irrigate only three times, but time them precisely: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I will spray once for weeds, once for powdery mildew, and once for aphids—three pesticide applications in total. If the weather cooperates, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

After wheat harvest in early June, every hour counts. I will plant a hybrid summer maize variety the same day using no-tillage seeding. Almost everyone in our village has switched to this for summer maize because there is no time to plough between crops, and it saves diesel and soil moisture. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress urea at the jointing stage, totaling about 18 kg of nitrogen, 4 kg of phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice: once at seedling establishment if June is dry, and once at silking. Two herbicide applications and one insecticide spray for corn borer will be enough. I expect about 550 kg per mu.
